title: The Constitution of India Made Simple
summary: What the Constitution is, who wrote it and what rights and duties it gives every citizen.

steps.title: The rule book
sentences: A constitution is the rule book of a country.
It says how the government works and what rights people have.
The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950, which we celebrate as Republic Day.

steps.title: Who wrote it?
sentences: A Constituent Assembly wrote it, and its work took nearly three years.
Dr B. R. Ambedkar was the chairman of the Drafting Committee, and Dr Rajendra Prasad was the president of the Assembly.
It is one of the longest written constitutions in the world.

steps.title: Big promises
sentences: The Preamble tells us what India promises: justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
India is described as sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic and a republic.
Every citizen has the same rights, whatever their religion, caste, gender or birthplace.

steps.title: Rights and duties
sentences: Fundamental Rights include the right to equality, the right to freedom, and the right to education for children aged 6 to 14.
There are also Fundamental Duties, such as respecting the flag and caring for the environment.
Rights and duties go together: we enjoy our rights when everyone does their duty.

facts: The original Constitution was handwritten and decorated by artists, not printed.
India's Constitution has been amended many times to meet new needs.
26 November is observed as Constitution Day, because the Constitution was adopted on that day in 1949.

quiz.q: When did the Constitution come into force?
quiz.why: It came into force on 26 January 1950, Republic Day.
Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

quiz.q: Which word is NOT in the list of Preamble promises?
quiz.why: The Preamble promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

notes: Based on the text of the Constitution of India; details such as amendments can change over time.
